source.name: Form fields inside a disabled fieldset must not be treated as tabbable, so a focus-trapped dialog focuses its first usable field
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/focus-trap/tabbable/issues/413) at cc8b7b2bc4319b672d0e6053b34c732168dd035c. Blind to the maintainers' fix 1d5fcb51d9eb21994c82a2f03010bc0d017cfff2; routing auto.

journey.title: Opening the address dialog puts focus on the first usable field
journey.goal: A keyboard user can open the dialog, type an address and save it

functionalJourney.title: Save the address dialog with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, saves and closes

success.value: Delivery address saved without a street.

functional.value: Delivery address saved without a street.

guards.title: Escape closes the address dialog and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: Focus does not move to the first input field when the dialog opens because the focus trap delays initial focus via a setTimeout, leaving focus on the triggering element.
plan.repair_strategy: Disable the delayInitialFocus option when creating the focus trap so that initial focus is applied synchronously after the dialog is shown.

edits.before: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; } });
edits.after: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; }, delayInitialFocus: false });

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will receive focus on the first usable field (#street) when the address dialog opens, meeting focus order expectations.
functional_risks: Setting focus synchronously could, in rare cases, occur before the dialog is fully rendered or before assistive technologies have announced it; however the dialog is already present in the DOM and only its hidden attribute is toggled, making this risk minimal.
verification_requirements: After pressing Enter on the #open button, focus must be on the #street input.
Pressing Tab from #street should move focus to the #save button.
Pressing Enter on #save should close the dialog and update the status field with the entered address.

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's initial focus is delayed by default (via setTimeout) and may not move focus synchronously after the dialog becomes visible, leaving focus on the triggering button. Additionally, the automatic first-tabstop detection might not run at the right time due to asynchronous activation.
plan.repair_strategy: Configure the focus trap to focus the street input immediately and synchronously by setting `initialFocus: '#street'` and `delayInitialFocus: false`.

edits.before: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; } });
edits.after: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; }, initialFocus: '#street', delayInitialFocus: false });

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will receive focus on the street input when the address dialog opens, meeting focus order expectations.
functional_risks: Setting focus synchronously could, in rare cases, occur before the dialog is fully rendered; however the dialog is already present in the DOM and only its hidden attribute is toggled, making this risk minimal.
verification_requirements: After pressing Enter on the #open button, focus must be on the #street input.
Pressing Tab from #street should move focus to the #save button.
Pressing Enter on #save should close the dialog and update the status field with the entered address.
